metadata.note: Macon, Dublin and Savannah: one 92-mile line, Macon - Dublin - Vidalia, GA, built in two stages (Macon - Dublin 1891/92, Dublin - Vidalia 1902). It never reached Savannah. Two features, one per drawable span, both MD&S-operated throughout (SAL stock control from 1907 was not operation, so no Rule 4 split); colour new to the dataset. No branches. Passenger service ended with the last trains of 31 Dec 1949.

geometry_sources.osm: OpenStreetMap, ODbL: Georgia Central Railway ways tagged old_railway_operator 'Macon, Dublin and Savannah;SAL;SCL' / 'Macon, Dublin and Savannah' (42 ways in the corridor)

not_yet_sourced: Macon - Dublin start: drawn from 1892 (first primary evidence, Savannah Morning News 6 Apr 1892; ICC completion 1 Jan 1892). Two local-history blogs date the first train to 21 or 22 July 1891; a contemporary 1891 newspaper (e.g. Macon Telegraph, July 1891) would be needed to move the start to 1891.
Last-train date: 31 Dec 1949 (company notice, Soperton News 22/29 Dec 1949) versus 1 Dec 1949 (Soperton News news story of 1 Dec 1949). Year 1949 either way.
1928 PSC ruling: printed as letting the road drop 17/18, yet the surviving pair from 1930 is numbered 17/18 (OCR garble or renumbering). Frequency only, not dates.
Headways (720 min to 1928, 1440 min after) are estimates from pair counts in scattered timetables and news items, not a full run of timetables; the 1922 strike suspension of 17/18 is not drawn.
avg_speed_kmh is an estimate; no MD&S running time was found.
Macon end: the last ~0.8 mi into Macon Terminal Station (and the pre-1916 8th and Cherry Streets station) is not drawn.
SAL formal absorption 1957 or 1958 (sources disagree); 1906 ACL control treated as stock-only. Neither affects drawn years.

properties.line: Macon, Dublin and Savannah: Macon – Dublin
properties.speed_source: estimated: no running time for the MD&S's own Macon - Vidalia trains was found. The only timing is the 1902 through-car service, Macon - Savannah 172 mi in 6.5 h (about 42 km/h) including the SAL's main line beyond Vidalia; a local stopping at some twenty stations on a light branch is taken to be slower, about 20 mph
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), ways tagged old_railway_operator='Macon, Dublin and Savannah;SAL;SCL' (and five tagged 'Macon, Dublin and Savannah'), today the Georgia Central Railway main line, e.g. ways 199426690, 164664151, 393623827, 429400468, 960083153; routed with opstrace.py
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 52.4 mi against documented about 53.5 mi (Fowler: Macon Terminal Station 92.3, Dublin 38.8 from Vidalia; ICC about 54 mi), 98% of documented. 51.9 mi of the routed line is on track tagged as the MD&S, 0.5 mi untagged connecting track. The Macon end stops where the MD&S-tagged track ends at the Georgia Central yard in east Macon, about 1.3 km (0.8 mi) short of Macon Terminal Station: the only surviving rail path from there to the station winds about 5.5 km through yards and NS/ex-CofG track, which would misstate the route, so that last stretch into the station (Terminal Station from 1916; 8th and Cherry Streets before that) is not drawn, and is most of the shortfall against the documented mileage. Waypoints Dry Branch, Fitzpatrick, Jeffersonville, Danville, Allentown and Montrose lie on the line; Dudley 0.7 km, Dublin town centre 0.3 km. Every leg is routed on OSM track; none is approximated. The alignment is today's Georgia Central Railway (ex-SAL/SCL/CSX Macon Subdivision); no relocation of the MD&S main line is recorded in the research report, so it is taken to be the 1892/1902 alignment, but the current track has not been checked against an early map and minor realignments cannot be ruled out.

segments.note: Macon - Dublin local passenger trains, two round trips a day (trains 17/18 and 19/20), which the Soperton News of 9 Dec 1927 says ran 'ever since the M. D. & S. railroad has been built'; the 1916 timetable (The Enterprise, 23 Nov 1917, Time Table No. 1 effective 18 Dec 1916) shows both pairs. Headway 720 min is an estimate from that pair count, not from a full run of timetables. 17/18 was taken off temporarily from 28 Jul 1922 in the shopmen's strike (Montgomery Monitor, 17 Aug 1922); that gap is not drawn. From 1902 these trains ran through to Vidalia (see the Dublin - Vidalia feature). Macon station was at 8th and Cherry Streets, then Macon Terminal Station from 1916. Start 1892 is collapsed from a source conflict: two local-history blogs date the first train to 21 or 22 July 1891 (secondary sources only), while the ICC valuation gives construction completed 1 Jan 1892 and the first primary evidence of regular trains is the Savannah Morning News of 6 Apr 1892 ('A mail service has been established over the Macon and Dublin railroad'). 1891 is not drawn. The company was the Macon and Dublin until the charter amendment of 11 Sep 1890. Ends 1928 when the Georgia PSC let the road drop one pair (Soperton News, 11 May 1928). Operated by the Macon, Dublin and Savannah with its own staff throughout; Seaboard Air Line interests held the stock from 1907 but did not run the trains (ICC valuation), so the feature is not split or coloured as the SAL. USRA federal control 28 Dec 1917 - 1 Mar 1920 is not split.
sources: Segment-level: start from Savannah Morning News 6 Apr 1892 p6 (mail service) and the ICC valuation (completed 1 Jan 1892); 1891 conflict from the Dublin/Laurens County history blog; headway from Soperton News 9 Dec 1927 and The Enterprise 23 Nov 1917 p3; end of two-pair service from Soperton News 4 and 11 May 1928 (GA Historic Newspapers), as read by the research report

segments.note: One round trip a day, numbered 17/18 in the 1930 and 1934 schedules printed in the Soperton News, after the Georgia PSC allowed one pair to be dropped in May 1928 (Soperton News, 11 May 1928; the ruling as printed names 17/18, the surviving pair is 17/18, unresolved). Headway 1440 min is an estimate from that pair count. Elliott Brack recalls riding the daily train Macon Terminal - Allentown about 1945. Ends 1949, exact: the company's notice in the Soperton News of 22 and 29 Dec 1949 says that, as authorized by the Georgia Public Service Commission order of 15 Nov 1949, the MD&S would discontinue passenger trains 17 and 18 between Macon and Vidalia 'effective with the last trains from terminals on December 31, 1949'. Source conflict: a Soperton News story of 1 Dec 1949 says the last trains were to come off that day; the company's later, more specific notice is preferred, and the year is 1949 either way. Trucks replaced the trains for mail and express; the Feb 1952 Official Guide prints the MD&S as 'Freight Service only'. Freight continued under the SAL (absorbed 1957 or 1958), SCL, CSX and, since 1990, the Georgia Central Railway; none of that is drawn (Rule 1). Operated by the Macon, Dublin and Savannah with its own staff throughout; Seaboard Air Line interests held the stock from 1907 but did not run the trains (ICC valuation), so the feature is not split or coloured as the SAL. USRA federal control 28 Dec 1917 - 1 Mar 1920 is not split.
sources: Segment-level: one daily pair from Soperton News 11 May 1928 and the 1930/1934 Soperton schedules; end from the MD&S discontinuance notice, Soperton News 22 and 29 Dec 1949 p4, and the Feb 1952 Official Guide, as read by the research report

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 39.0 mi against documented 38.8 mi (Fowler; ICC about 38 mi; Savannah Morning News 9 Apr 1902 'thirty eight miles'), 101% of documented. 38.8 mi of the routed line is on MD&S-tagged track, 0.3 mi untagged at the ends. Runs from the same Dublin point where the Macon - Dublin feature ends to the Vidalia station area at the junction with the SAL Savannah - Montgomery line; every waypoint (Catlin, Minter, Rockledge, Orland, Soperton, Tarrytown, Kibbee, Vidalia) is within 0.3 km of the line. At Dublin the trace stays off the crossing ex-Central of Georgia / Wrightsville and Tennille lines (all MD&S-tagged mileage). Every leg is routed on OSM track; none is approximated. The alignment is today's Georgia Central Railway (ex-SAL/SCL/CSX Macon Subdivision); no relocation of the MD&S main line is recorded in the research report, so it is taken to be the 1892/1902 alignment, but the current track has not been checked against an early map and minor realignments cannot be ruled out.

segments.note: Dublin - Vidalia extension, opened 1902: last spike 28 Jan 1902 (Savannah Morning News, 30 Jan 1902); a passenger train was to run Saturday 1 Feb 1902 (Atlanta Semi-Weekly Journal, 3 Feb 1902); 'the first train between Macon [and] Vidalia ... came through last night' (Macon News in Savannah Morning News, 2 Apr 1902); ICC gives construction 1 Apr 1901 - 1 Apr 1902. From 17 Aug 1902 MD&S cars ran on to Savannah in SAL trains (Savannah Morning News, 10 and 18 Aug 1902); the Vidalia - Savannah leg is the SAL's line and is not drawn here. Two round trips a day Macon - Vidalia as on the Macon - Dublin section; headway 720 min is an estimate from that pair count. Ends 1928 when one pair was dropped (Soperton News, 11 May 1928). Operated by the Macon, Dublin and Savannah with its own staff throughout; Seaboard Air Line interests held the stock from 1907 but did not run the trains (ICC valuation), so the feature is not split or coloured as the SAL. USRA federal control 28 Dec 1917 - 1 Mar 1920 is not split.
